criteria.justification: The response immediately commits to “roll back (disable/feature-flag off) the new integration launch right now” and makes that the first concrete action.

It explicitly characterizes rollback as a “known, bounded action” and reversible through a later relaunch, while noting that ongoing customer-trust damage is less reversible. However, it does not directly contrast rollback with the uncertainty and difficult recovery involved in attempting an unvalidated fast patch.

It directly weighs compounding incorrect alerts, support burden, and trust erosion against the “reputational/scheduling friction” of pausing a publicly announced feature, concluding that the former is substantially more harmful.
The response chooses immediate rollback rather than rushing a patch and explicitly reserves the “proper, well-tested fix” for a follow-up project before relaunch.

It provides specific follow-through: verify rollback effectiveness, communicate separately with affected existing customers and new-integration customers, notify the manager asynchronously, build the proper fix, plan the relaunch, and conduct a retrospective.
